_meta.name: Warli grammar rules
_meta.description: Rule-based grammar layer applied after dictionary lookup: word-order reordering, inflection/affixation, postposition mapping, negation, and tense cues.

word_order._comment: Warli, like Marathi/Hindi, is predominantly SOV (subject-object-verb). The reorderer moves verbs to the end and keeps the subject first.

function_words._comment: Purely grammatical source words that have no Warli output token: articles, the copula, and tense auxiliaries. They are DROPPED during lookup instead of being echoed back in the source language. They still drive `cue_rules`, because those match against the raw source tokens. Relational words (in/on/to/with/for/from/at/by ...) are deliberately NOT listed here — they resolve through `postpositions`. The modals (would/could/should/may/might/must) are NOT here either; they carry real meaning and live in the dictionary. Warli, like Marathi, routinely omits the present copula, so dropping is/am/are/है/हूँ is linguistically correct and also stops the copula from absorbing a tense suffix ('is' -> 'आहेता').

inflections._comment: Affixes keyed by a coarse grammatical feature, applied to the Warli verb token when the matching source cue is detected. Keys ending in '_prefix' are PREPENDED by the engine, all others are appended. Pluralization is deliberately absent: Warli/Marathi plurals are irregular (पोर->पोरां, शेळी->शेळ्या, झाड->झाडां) and are stored as real headwords in warli_dictionary.json instead of being generated by one suffix.

postpositions._comment: English/Hindi relational words mapped to Warli postpositions (Warli uses postpositions, not prepositions).

cue_rules._comment: Hindi progressive 'रहा/रही/रहे'. No English cue: the tokenizer splits on whitespace so a bare 'ing' can never match a token — English progressive is covered by the am/is/are rule above.
